Get Covariate Statistics for Forest Plots

getCovStats.Rd

Quickly generates a list of summary statistics for specified covariates, formatted for use in forest plots. The function handles continuous, binary, and multi-level categorical variables differently based on their number of unique values.

Usage

getCovStats(
  data,
  covariates,
  minLevels = 10,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.95),
  idVar = "ID",
  missVal = -99,
  nsig = 3,
  catRef = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  refLevels = NULL,
  sep = "_"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame that includes the covariates to summarise. Only the first record per subject (identified by idVar) will be used.

covariates

A character vector of covariate names as they appear in the data frame.

minLevels

The maximum number of unique values a covariate can have to be treated as categorical. Covariates with more unique values than minLevels are treated as continuous. Default is 10.

probs

A numeric vector of two probabilities used to calculate quantiles for continuous covariates. Defaults to c(0.05, 0.95).

idVar

The name of the subject identifier column, used to select one record per subject. Defaults to "ID".

missVal

The value indicating missing data, which will be excluded from calculations. Defaults to -99.

nsig

The number of significant digits (passed to the signif function) for rounding the summary of continuous covariates. Defaults to 3.

catRef

The reference level for multi-level categorical covariates - the level represented by the all-zero one-hot row. Either a single setting applied to every covariate or a named list with an optional default component; each entry is a level, "lowest" (the default), "mode" or "model". For example list(GENO = 2). Has no effect on continuous or binary covariates.

model

The NONMEM control stream, required when catRef is "model". Either a path to the .mod file or the list returned by createParamFunction().

refLevels

Deprecated. Use catRef.

sep

The separator between the covariate name and the level in the one-hot column names for multi-level categorical covariates. Defaults to "_", matching the NONMEM FREM convention.

Value

A list where each element corresponds to a covariate.

  • For continuous covariates, the element is a named numeric vector of quantiles.

  • For binary covariates, the element is a sorted vector of the two unique values.

  • For multi-level categorical covariates, the element is a nested list of one-hot encoded vectors. The reference level (the lowest level, or the one named in catRef) is represented by all vectors being 0.

Examples

dfData <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "SimVal/DAT-1-MI-PMX-2.csv", package = "PMXForest")
)

# Continuous covariates -> quantiles; binary -> the two levels;
# GENO (4 levels) -> a one-hot list with level 1 as the reference.
getCovStats(dfData, covariates = c("WT", "AGE", "SEX", "GENO"), idVar = "ID")
#> $WT
#>    5%   95% 
#>  58.5 126.0 
#> 
#> $AGE
#>  5% 95% 
#>  22  65 
#> 
#> $SEX
#> [1] 1 2
#> 
#> $GENO
#> $GENO$GENO_2
#> [1] 0 1 0 0
#> 
#> $GENO$GENO_3
#> [1] 0 0 1 0
#> 
#> $GENO$GENO_4
#> [1] 0 0 0 1
#> 
#> 

# Non-default quantiles and rounding for a continuous covariate
getCovStats(dfData, "CRCL", idVar = "ID", probs = c(0.1, 0.9), nsig = 4)
#> $CRCL
#>    10%    90% 
#>  83.66 150.00 
#> 

# Use genotype level 2 as the reference instead of the lowest level
getCovStats(dfData, "GENO", idVar = "ID", catRef = list(GENO = 2))
#> $GENO
#> $GENO$GENO_1
#> [1] 1 0 0 0
#> 
#> $GENO$GENO_3
#> [1] 0 0 1 0
#> 
#> $GENO$GENO_4
#> [1] 0 0 0 1
#> 
#>
